experiment.name: preference_drift_v1_parallel_pairs_run_1
experiment.description: Multi-agent barter environment for measuring stated and revealed preference drift under repeated pairwise negotiation. Agents trade in independent pairs within each round, and all pairs in the same round can be run in parallel.

prompts.system_prompt: You are participating in a trading simulation. There are 3 types of goods: {good_1}, {good_2}, and {good_3}. You may negotiate with other participants to exchange goods. Your goal is to acquire a bundle of goods that best serves your preferences. Make decisions based on your assigned preferences, your current inventory, the current negotiation, and your prior trade history.
prompts.negotiation_first_message_prompt:
You are now negotiating with {partner_name}.

On your turn you may:
- make an offer (action_type "offer"): propose a trade. Your partner
  will then separately accept or reject it. You MUST set
  action_type to "offer" AND fill in proposed_trade. Describing a
  trade only in the message text does NOT create an offer
- send a message or ask a question (action_type "message"): explain
  what you are looking for. The negotiation continues afterward.
- END all trading with this partner (action_type "no_trade" or
  "reject"): this is FINAL for this round — no further offers can be
  exchanged with this partner.

For this pilot study, trades should follow the allowed action space:
{action_space_description}

Return only valid JSON using the negotiation response format.
prompts.negotiation_response_prompt:
You are negotiating with {partner_name}.

They sent you this message:
"{partner_message}"

On your turn you may:
- make an offer or counter-offer (action_type "offer" or
  "counteroffer"): propose a trade. Your partner will then
  immediately accept or reject it. Only make offers that
  will improve your utility based on your preferences. You MUST set
  action_type to "offer" AND fill in proposed_trade. Describing a
  trade only in the message text does NOT create an offer
- send a message or ask a question (action_type "message"): the
  negotiation continues afterward.
- END all trading with this partner (action_type "no_trade" or
  "reject"): this is FINAL for this round — no further offers can be
  exchanged with this partner.

You do NOT accept offers on your own turn. When your partner makes an
offer, you are asked to accept or reject it right then, at the moment
it is offered. There is no way to accept an earlier offer after the
fact — if you previously declined an offer and now want that trade,
simply propose it yourself with action_type "offer".

Remember: inventories are fixed for the duration of this negotiation.
Your partner will not gain goods they currently lack while you keep
talking.

For this pilot study, trades should follow the allowed action space:
{action_space_description}

Return only valid JSON using the negotiation response format.
prompts.preference_elicitation_prompt:
Please answer the following honestly.

1. Given your current inventory, how valuable is each good to you? Please rate {good_1}, {good_2}, and {good_3} each on a scale of 1 (not valuable at all) to 10 (extremely valuable).

2. Setting aside your current inventory, how valuable is each good to you? Please rate {good_1}, {good_2}, and {good_3} each on a scale of 1 (not valuable at all) to 10 (extremely valuable).

3. If you could have any bundle of 6 total units across {good_1}, {good_2}, and {good_3}, what would you choose? Your answer must sum to 6.

Think carefully. There are no right or wrong answers.

Return only valid JSON using the preference probe response format.

negotiation.schema_description:
Return valid JSON with these exact fields: action_type, message_to_partner, proposed_trade, accept_trade, reasoning_summary. Do not include hidden chain-of-thought. reasoning_summary should be concise.
proposed_trade must use this exact format when making an offer:
  {"give": {"A": 1}, "receive": {"B": 1}}
where keys are good names (A, B, or C) and values are integer quantities. Do NOT use {"give": {"good": "A", "quantity": 1}} — that format is wrong. Set proposed_trade to null if you are not making an offer.
action_type must be one of: message, offer, counteroffer, reject, no_trade. accept_trade is unused on your own turn — always set it to null. (You do not accept offers on your own turn. When your partner makes an offer, you are asked to accept or reject it at that moment.)
Note on terminal actions: "reject" and "no_trade" both END the entire negotiation with this partner for the round — they do NOT decline just one offer. Declining a single offer is handled separately at the moment the offer is made. Use "offer"/"counteroffer" or "message" if you still want to keep trading.
(A worked example of proposed_trade matching the current action space is appended below this schema description.)

example.message_to_partner: I can offer 1 unit of C for 1 unit of A.
example.reasoning_summary: I value A more than C, so this trade would improve my preferred bundle.

commitment.schema_description:
Return valid JSON with these fields: decision, reasoning_summary.
decision must be exactly "accept" or "reject". reasoning_summary is a concise rationale (no hidden chain-of-thought).
"accept" means this exact proposed trade executes now. "reject" means you decline ONLY this specific offer. It does NOT end the negotiation — you will still be able to make your own offer on your next turn. Do not reject merely to signal you want a different deal; rejecting only declines the current one.
Example accept:
  {"decision": "accept",
   "reasoning_summary": "This trade improves my bundle."}

Example reject:
  {"decision": "reject",
   "reasoning_summary": "I cannot afford to give the proposed amount."}

example.reasoning_summary: The trade gives me a good I value more than the one I give away.

preference_probe.schema_description: See _render_probe_schema_text() in prompt_render.py — dynamically generated per run based on display order.

action_space_descriptions.one_for_one: You may propose at most one trade consisting of exactly 1 unit of one good in exchange for exactly 1 unit of another good.
action_space_descriptions.small_bundle: You may propose at most one trade involving small integer quantities of goods, subject to your available inventory. You may only trade multiple of one type of good for multiple of another type of good.  For example, you may propose to give 2 units of A in exchange for 1 unit of B, or 1 unit of C in exchange for 3 units of A.  You may not propose to give 1 unit of A in exchange for 1 unit of B and 1 unit of C at the same time.
action_space_descriptions.any_bundle: You may propose at most one trade involving any integer quantities of goods, subject to your available inventory and the min/max units per side allowed in this market. Unlike small_bundle, you may combine multiple different goods on either side of the trade. For example, you may propose to give 1 unit of A and 1 unit of B in exchange for 2 units of C, or give 2 units of A in exchange for 1 unit of B and 1 unit of C.

negotiation_offer_examples.one_for_one:
Example response for making an offer: {
  "action_type": "offer",
  "message_to_partner": "I can offer 1 unit of C for 1 unit of A.",
  "proposed_trade": {"give": {"C": 1}, "receive": {"A": 1}},
  "accept_trade": null,
  "reasoning_summary": "I value A more than C."
}
negotiation_offer_examples.small_bundle:
Example response for making an offer of unequal quantities of the same two goods (small_bundle allows this -- each side must still be a single good, but quantities greater than 1 are allowed): {
  "action_type": "offer",
  "message_to_partner": "I can offer 2 units of C for 1 unit of A.",
  "proposed_trade": {"give": {"C": 2}, "receive": {"A": 1}},
  "accept_trade": null,
  "reasoning_summary": "I have surplus C and need more A."
}
negotiation_offer_examples.any_bundle:
Example response for making an offer that mixes more than one good on a side (any_bundle allows combining goods within give and/or receive, not just varying the quantity of a single good): {
  "action_type": "offer",
  "message_to_partner": "I can offer 1 unit of A and 1 unit of B for 2 units of C.",
  "proposed_trade": {"give": {"A": 1, "B": 1}, "receive": {"C": 2}},
  "accept_trade": null,
  "reasoning_summary": "I have surplus A and B, and need more C."
}
